title: Biscuits and Gravy
subtitle: Southern American buttermilk biscuits with sausage cream gravy
excerpt: Biscuits and gravy is a Southern American breakfast of flaky buttermilk biscuits (closer to British scones than anything else) split and smothered in a thick, creamy white sauce made from crumbled pork sausage, flour, milk, and black pepper. It is an intensely filling dish, deeply savoury and comforting.
sourceNotes: Biscuits and gravy is a staple of Southern and Appalachian American cooking. The dish dates to the 19th century when affordable pork sausage and flour gravy were practical foods for working families. It remains a defining dish of the American South and Midwest.

recipe.batchNotes: Biscuits can be baked in large batches. The gravy is best made fresh.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Biscuits are best eaten fresh from the oven. The gravy can be made 1 hour ahead and reheated with a splash of milk.

content.text: American biscuits and British scones are close relatives: both are quick-leavened breads made by rubbing fat into flour. The differences are small: American biscuits use more fat, tend to be less sweet, and are cut thicker. The gravy is a white sauce (béchamel base) with crumbled sausage meat and a heavy hand with black pepper.

items.prepNote: 300 g for biscuits, 30 g for gravy

content.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Mix the flour, baking powder, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture looks like rough breadcrumbs. Stir in the buttermilk with a fork until just combined: the dough will look shaggy and rough. Do not overwork it.

Turn onto a floured surface and pat (not roll) to about 2.5 cm thick. Cut into rounds with a 7 cm cutter, pressing straight down without twisting. Place on a lined baking tray with the biscuits touching. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until risen and golden. The touching sides help them rise upright.
While the biscuits bake, cook the crumbled sausage meat in a dry frying pan over high heat, breaking it up with a spoon, for 6 to 8 minutes until well browned.

Reduce the heat to medium. Scatter the flour over the sausage and stir for 1 minute. Gradually pour in the milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until thick and creamy. Season very generously with black pepper and salt. A good gravy is aggressively peppery. Add a dash of hot sauce if using.
Split the warm biscuits and place two on each plate. Ladle the gravy generously over the top.

items.symptom: Biscuits are dense and did not rise
items.cause: Dough was overworked, developing the gluten and making the biscuits tough
items.fix: Handle the dough as little as possible. Mix until just combined and pat rather than roll.

items.cause: Milk was added too fast or too cold before the flour had fully absorbed
items.fix: Add the milk in a thin stream while stirring constantly. If lumps form, whisk vigorously or pass through a sieve.

content.text: Biscuits and gravy is associated with the American South: Virginia, Tennessee, Georgia, the Carolinas. It is a breakfast dish first, though diners serve it all day. The cheap cut of pork used for the sausage and the simplicity of flour gravy made it a practical food for communities where money was scarce, and it has remained central to Southern food culture.
